edge_cases: Invalid YAML syntax in /library/add_book results in a 400 error.
Missing required fields (title, author, isbn) or non‑integer year cause a 400 error on add.
Omitting the 'isbn' parameter on remove, update, or info endpoints yields a 400 error.
Providing wrong admin credentials returns a 401 Unauthorized response.
Calling /admin/change_password with an incorrect old password returns a 401 error.
The inventory check endpoint runs a script regardless of the validity of 'section' or 'location' parameters.
contract.intent: Provide a simple library management HTTP API with endpoints to add, remove, query, and update book records, perform an inventory check, and handle admin authentication and password changes.
invariants: A book must include non‑empty 'title', 'author', and 'isbn' fields to be added.
The 'year_published' field must be an integer; otherwise the add request is rejected.
Admin login succeeds only when both password and secret_key match the expected constants.
The password change succeeds only if the provided old password matches the current LIBRARIAN_PASSWORD.
All responses are JSON objects with a 'status' field indicating success or error.
io_behavior: POST /library/add_book expects raw YAML in the request body and returns JSON with book details or error messages.
POST /library/remove_book expects form field 'isbn' and returns JSON confirming removal or error.
GET /inventory/check expects query parameters 'section' and 'location' and returns JSON indicating the check was started.
POST /admin/login expects form fields 'password' and 'secret_key' and returns JSON granting or denying admin access.
POST /admin/change_password expects form fields 'old_password' and 'new_password' and returns JSON indicating success or failure.
GET /library/book_info, /library/update_book, and /library/list_books return JSON with static or echoed book information based on query or form parameters.
side_effects: Executes an external Python script via os.system when /inventory/check is called.
Updates the in‑memory LIBRARIAN_PASSWORD variable when the admin changes the password.
None of the endpoints persist data to disk or a database; all responses are generated at request time.

rationale: All endpoints follow the specified I/O and invariants, returning JSON with a status field and handling required/invalid inputs correctly, except the inventory check endpoint validates parameters before invoking the external script, violating the contract that the script runs regardless of parameter validity.
